prose: Injecting 3.5% potable water into dry 12.0% hard winter wheat hydrated the fibrous pericarp and aleurone layers. The toughened bran resisted shattering during break passes, peeling away in broad flakes that kept the flour snow-white.

Holding damp wheat in timber rest bins for eighteen hours allowed moisture to diffuse evenly from the outer husk into the starchy endosperm. Cross-sectional kernel cuts confirmed uniform translucency with zero dry white cores.

Washing grain with 52°C water inside a high-speed whizzer scourer stripped surface soil and fungal spores while accelerating water absorption. The rapid hydrothermal conditioning cut required bin dwell time from 24 hours down to eight hours.

Tempering hard vitreous durum wheat to 15.2% moisture mellowed the gluten-starch protein matrix. Roller mill grinding power consumption dropped by 18%, and mechanical starch granule damage remained within optimal baking limits (6.5%).

A malfunctioning flowmeter overdosed water to 6.5%, driving wheat moisture to 18.5%. The soggy grain transformed into sticky dough paste between the first break rolls, packing solid into the spiral fluting and choking the millstand.

Hurling tempered grain at 90 m/s against hardened steel impact pins inside the entoleter shattered microscopic insect eggs and larvae inside hidden kernel crevices. Sound wheat berries rebounded undamaged, ensuring insect-free storage.

An intensive rotor dampener with angled mixing paddles whipped wheat kernels through a 4-bar atomized water spray. High-velocity berry-to-berry friction forced water into the kernel creases, achieving uniform moisture uptake across eight tons per hour.
